source.author: lucr
source.text: iuvat integros accedere fontis atque haurire iuvatque novos decerpere flores insignemque meo capiti petere inde coronam, unde prius nulli velarint tempora Musae; primum quod magnis doceo de rebus et artis religionum animum nodis exsolvere pergo, deinde quod obscura de re tam lucida pango carmina musaeo contingens cuncta lepore.
source.text_original: iuvat integros accedere fontis / atque haurire iuvatque novos decerpere flores / insignemque meo capiti petere inde coronam, / unde prius nulli velarint tempora Musae; / primum quod magnis doceo de rebus et artis / religionum animum nodis exsolvere pergo, / deinde quod obscura de re tam lucida pango / carmina musaeo contingens cuncta lepore.
source.text_english: It delights me to approach the untouched springs and it delights me to draw from them and pluck new flowers, and then to seek for my head a crown distinguished by the place from which the Muses have first veiled no one’s temples before; first because I teach about great matters and go on to release the mind from the knotted bonds of religion, then because on a subject so obscure I compose such clear verses, touching everything with the Muses’ charm.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: magnum hoc opus et homine dignum, religionum animos nodis exsoluere pergo, ut ait Lucretius, qui quidem hoc efficere non poterat, quia nihil ueri afferebat.
reuse.text_original: magnum hoc opus et homine dignum, religionum animos nodis exsoluere pergo, ut ait Lucretius, qui quidem hoc efficere non poterat, quia nihil ueri afferebat.
reuse.text_english: I go on to untie minds from the knots of religions, as Lucretius says, a great work and one worthy of a man; though he certainly could not accomplish this, because he brought forward nothing true.
